name: Progesterone receptor (PR)
summary: Progesterone receptor expression is an ER-regulated gene product that refines prognosis within hormone receptor-positive breast cancer; it is routinely reported alongside ER and HER2.
biology: PGR is transcriptionally induced by ER signalling, so PR expression partly reflects a functional ER pathway. PR loss in ER-positive tumours has been associated with growth factor receptor and PI3K pathway activation and a more aggressive, luminal B-like phenotype.
alterations: PR-negative (in ER-positive disease, associated with higher risk)

methods: Immunohistochemistry for nuclear PR with ASCO/CAP-aligned scoring
testing.notes: Isolated ER-negative/PR-positive results are uncommon and may reflect technical artefact; repeat testing is advised.

predictiveRelevance: PR is primarily prognostic; endocrine therapy decisions rest on ER status. Low or absent PR in ER-positive disease contributes to luminal B classification and may inform decisions on chemotherapy and treatment escalation alongside genomic assays.
